title: Understanding Your IT Manager Salary: Hourly to Annual Conversion
description: Convert your IT manager salary from hourly to annual using a 38-hour week. Includes tax, super, casual loading, and award coverage guidance from Fair Work.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, assume 38 hours per week. For example, $50/hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $98,800 per year. The [the timesheet](/) tool does this automatically and also shows fortnightly pay, tax, and super.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates for IT managers?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage (NMW) from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. However, most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. IT managers may be award-free if they are qualified professionals not in the IT or telecommunications industry, as per. Award-free employees are entitled to the NMW and National Employment Standards, but actual IT manager salaries are typically much higher, often exceeding the ABS average weekly earnings of $2,083.70 for full-time adults.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my pay as an IT manager?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. If you are a casual IT manager, your employer may pay a casual rate that already includes loading, or they may pay the base rate plus loading separately. On [the timesheet](/) you enter your base hourly rate and check the 'casual loading' box to add 25% on top. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting an IT Manager Salary from Hourly to Annual

When you see an hourly rate for an IT manager role, it can be helpful to convert it to an annual salary to compare offers or budget your income. The standard formula used in Australia is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For full-time work, we assume a 38-hour week, which is the ordinary hours under the National Employment Standards (NES) and most modern awards. This assumption is built into [the timesheet](/) calculator. If your role is part-time or you work different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

### Example: IT Manager on $70 per hour

- Weekly pay: $70 × 38 = $2,660
- Fortnightly pay: $2,660 × 2 = $5,320
- Annual gross: $2,660 × 52 = $138,320

This is before tax, Medicare levy, and superannuation. The calculator on [the timesheet](/) also estimates these deductions.

## Award Coverage and Minimum Rates for IT Managers

Not all IT managers are covered by a modern award. According to the Fair Work Ombudsman, qualified IT employees who do not work for an employer in the IT or telecommunications services industry are often award-free. This means they are entitled only to the National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) and the NES. However, most IT managers earn well above this minimum.

If you are covered by an award (for example, the Professional Employees Award if you work in IT services), the award sets minimum pay rates, allowances, and penalty rates. You can check your award using the [pay guides](/blog) on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.

### Casual Loading for IT Managers

If you work as a casual IT manager, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave. On [the timesheet](/) you enter your base hourly rate (the rate before loading) and tick the 'casual loading' checkbox. The calculator then adds 25% to show your casual rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

## Tax and Superannuation on Your IT Manager Salary

### Income Tax (2026–27 Resident Rates)

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page explains how these apply.

### Superannuation Guarantee

Your employer must pay superannuation of 12% of your ordinary earnings on top of your salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For example, on a $138,320 annual salary, the super contribution would be $16,598.40, paid in addition to your salary. This is not deducted from your pay. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

## Comparing IT Manager Salaries with Industry Benchmarks

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time earnings was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026. That equates to about $108,352 annually. Many IT manager salaries are above this average, especially in senior roles or in industries like finance and technology.

When you use [the timesheet](/) to convert your hourly rate, you can compare your estimated annual pay with these benchmarks. Remember that the calculator assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice. Actual pay may differ.

## Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many Australian employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. For the $70/hour IT manager example:

- Weekly: $2,660
- Fortnightly: $5,320

This can help you plan your budget and compare with job advertisements that quote fortnightly or annual figures.

## Important Notes on the Calculator

The annual pay shown on [the timesheet](/) is an estimate based on the formula hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It does not account for unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For personalised advice, consult a qualified accountant or use the official tools from the Australian Taxation Office and Fair Work Ombudsman.
